messages:
Maya Chen: heads up — deploy to prod started ~5m ago (feature-flag rollout). seeing a quick SLO burn on inference.latency.p50 in the canary pool. not yet sure on customer impact. paging oncall.
SRE-Bot: Incident opened (P1) — Rapid SLO burn detected for inference.latency.p50 in canary. Pager routed to eng-oncall. Incident ID: INC-202403-874.
Tom R: on it. which canary? link to dashboard?
Maya Chen: canary-3. dashboards for per-canary broken; metrics page says 404 for the canary tag. looks like metrics ingestion changed tags in this deploy.
Gaurav Patel: wait — we pushed a small metrics rename in the rollout (env=canary -> deployment=canary) to standardize labels. I thought this would be opt-in.
Liz H: omg that explains why alerts fired differently. ops-bot shows alert was for `inference.latency.p50{env=canary}` and there were no series after deploy, then fallback alerts triggered on global SLO.
Tom R: paging got noisy because alert dedupe failed when series vanished. some people got paged twice via pageservice and oncall.
Kate Morales: customers reporting 500s? I see a handful of 500s in the last 3m on the API gateway logs but not widespread. link: https://logs.internal/r/abcd1234
Maya Chen: canary traffic spiked to 2x for short window — suspected because rollout ramp did a burst erroneously.
SRE-Bot: Runbook -> rollback flag: feature_flag/ff-feature-x kill -> POST /flags/feature-x/kill || Command: `curl -XPOST https://flags/api/kill/feature-x`
Tom R: let's kill the flag and pause rollout. @Gaurav can you flip kill now?
Gaurav Patel: doing it. `curl -XPOST ...` returned 200. flag is killed.
ops-bot: Feature flag feature-x set to KILLED by Gaurav Patel. Rollout paused.
Liz H: alert noise halting but SLO still showing burn because datapoints missing — the dashboard aggregates by old tag. can't trust the per-canary chart.
Kate Morales: we should validate customer impact: I pulled a sample from access logs; ~14 requests returned 500 across 10 customers, some retries. Not a full outage.
Tom R: good. next step: rollback to previous release for canary-3? or redeploy metrics shim to keep old tag aliasing?
Maya Chen: shorter path is to redeploy a sidecar that emits the old tag for a transitional 10m. I can push the shim quickly.
Gaurav Patel: agree — less blast radius than full rollback. but we still need to reconcile the metric rename in CI before further rollouts.
Liz H: putting a short-term pager quiet for the noisy dedupe — will silence the global SLO alert for 10m while we stabilize. react :hourglass_flowing_sand:.
SRE-Bot: Alert silenced for 10 minutes by Liz H.
Tom R: Maya — can you post the `kubectl` snippet you'll apply?
Maya Chen: applying now: ```kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: metrics-tag-alias
data:
  emit_env_tag: "canary"
EOF
```
Maya Chen: patch applied to canary-3. waiting for metrics to reappear.
Kate Morales: logs show service 502 -> 200 transitions after feature flag kill and configmap applied. still a few errors but trending down.
Gaurav Patel: pushing a patch to CI to gate tag rename behind a feature flag and add an automated tag-alias migration. PR: https://git.internal/p/5678
Tom R: thanks. can we confirm alerts stop firing before un-silencing?
Liz H: I'm monitoring. noise stopped but SLO latency p50 still shows elevated for the 6m window. should decay after datapoints roll in.
SRE-Bot: Incident INC-202403-874 updated: mitigate actions applied (flag kill, tag alias).
Maya Chen: quick postmortem notes — root cause: metrics tag rename shipped to canary without gating; rollout ramp bursted traffic due to ramp config bug; alerting rules didn't handle missing series gracefully -> duplicates/noisy pages; dashboards depended on old tag name.
Tom R: actions: 1) add metric rename gate + migration (Gaurav) 2) fix ramp logic to respect max-increase (Maya) 3) make alerts resilient to absent series (Liz) 4) improve pager dedupe when series vanish (SRE) 5) doc runbook for tag renames (Kate).
Gaurav Patel: I created the PR and added a test for ingestion aliasing. assigning to Maya for rollout plan.
Liz H: I'll open an alerting ticket for dedupe logic: ALERT-234.
ops-bot: Linked INC-202403-874 to ALERT-234 and PR-5678.
Tom R: thanks everyone. I'll keep the incident open until metrics fully backfilled and no new pages in 30m. then we'll transition to postmortem.
